fields.hero_prompt: Build a fintech landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a fintech landing page?
How do I create a fintech landing page?

plan.angle: Searchers for fintech landing page get design galleries (Behance, Dribbble), Figma community templates and one examples roundup: screenshots of fintech pages with nothing behind the button. This page shows four fintech landing pages built around what happens after the click (a waitlist that shows each signup its spot in line, a demo form that routes by monthly card volume, a pricing page that computes the fee before asking for an email, an early-access page that saves which link sent each signup), each with the form, the rule and the database row behind it, then gives the build steps. It makes no rate, APR, deposit, licensing or compliance claims and gives no financial or legal advice. SaaS, startup, CRM, developer and crypto pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
tab_stories: Harborlane's waitlist page shows that 2,417 people are already in line, and a new signup gets spot 2,418 on the confirmation screen and a row in the database.
Brackenpay asks for monthly card volume on its demo form and sends every request over $50,000 a month to Dana Merced; this month 9 of 31 requests went to her and 22 got the onboarding email.
Crestfield's pricing page does the fee math before the form asks for anything: a visitor who enters $8,000 in monthly card sales sees $232 a month at 2.9%, and the estimate saves with the email.
Ashwell promoted its early-access page through two links, and each signup saves the tag of the link that sent it: 37 of its 58 requests came from the podcast link and 21 from the newsletter link.
openers: Brackenpay wants a sales call only when the volume earns one
Crestfield answers the one question a shop owner arrived with
Ashwell ran the same offer through two links
Pick the one action the page asks for
Money raises the bar for proof
A visitor who types a dollar amount is qualifying
Keep the form as short as the ask
Route the request while the visitor is still reading
Write the headline around the account, not the company
Send a test signup from a phone
heading_shapes: Every signup sees the line it just joined (what the visitor sees, no number)
A $50,000 cutoff splits the demo queue (the threshold as subject)
The page does the fee math before the email ask (sequence: compute, then ask)
Each early-access row names the link that sent it (the record as subject)
